stimuli.title: Seven people live on different floors of a seven-storey building. Floor 1 is the bottom floor, and floor 7 is the top floor.
stimuli.body:
Clues:
1. There are exactly 1 positions between Lakshya and Geeta.
2. Pooja is exactly 2 positions above Ojas.
3. Vikram is exactly 3 positions above Mohan.
4. Geeta is at floor 1.
stimuli.solution: floor 1: Geeta; floor 2: Mohan; floor 3: Lakshya; floor 4: Ojas; floor 5: Vikram; floor 6: Pooja; floor 7: Nisha

stimuli.title: Seven labelled boxes are stacked vertically, with one box in each position.
stimuli.body:
Clues:
1. Ojas is exactly 3 positions above Rohan.
2. In the stated ordering, Ojas comes before Tanvi, and Tanvi comes before Deepa.
3. There are exactly 2 positions between Harish and Tanvi.
4. Yash is at position 6 from the bottom.
stimuli.solution: position 1 from the bottom: Rohan; position 2 from the bottom: Harish; position 3 from the bottom: Aarav; position 4 from the bottom: Ojas; position 5 from the bottom: Tanvi; position 6 from the bottom: Yash; position 7 from the bottom: Deepa

stimuli.title: Seven people have interviews in seven consecutive months from January to July, one per month.
stimuli.body:
Clues:
1. Lakshya is at April.
2. In the stated ordering, Lakshya comes before Ojas, and Ojas comes before Isha.
3. Uma is exactly 2 positions later than Tanvi.
4. Kavya is exactly 3 positions later than Uma.
stimuli.solution: January: Tanvi; February: Uday; March: Uma; April: Lakshya; May: Ojas; June: Kavya; July: Isha

stimuli.title: Seven employees hold seven distinct ranks (rank 1 is junior-most and rank 7 is senior-most).
stimuli.body:
Clues:
1. Uday is immediately senior to Kavya.
2. Geeta is at rank 7.
3. Meera is exactly 2 positions senior to Zoya.
4. Ravi is exactly 3 positions senior to Meera.
stimuli.solution: rank 1: Zoya; rank 2: Tarun; rank 3: Meera; rank 4: Kavya; rank 5: Uday; rank 6: Ravi; rank 7: Geeta

stimuli.title: In a certain coded language, each word has one unique code.
stimuli.body:
feather market planet = ka fi sa
golden planet mango = fi te bi
feather golden silver = mu ka bi
mango silver market = te mu sa
stimuli.solution: planet=fi, feather=ka, market=sa, golden=bi, mango=te, silver=mu

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Q > V ≤ R < X < U, decide which conclusions follow. I: Q < R. II: Q > V.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Q < P < T ≥ S = X, decide which conclusions follow. I: P < S. II: Q > S.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain T ≤ Z ≤ S > U > R, decide which conclusions follow. I: T ≤ Z. II: T > Z.

questions.stem: Statements: Some workers are drivers. Some drivers are farmers. Conclusions: I. Some workers are farmers. II. Some drivers are workers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows

questions.stem: Statements: All farmers are poets. Some workers are farmers. Conclusions: I. Some workers are poets. II. Some poets are workers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The existing C∩A members must lie in B, proving both conclusions.

questions.stem: Statements: No bakers are sailors. All artists are sailors. Some artists are sailors. Conclusions: I. No bakers are artists. II. Some artists are not bakers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: All C members belong to B, disjoint from A; some C are explicitly given.

questions.stem: Statements: Some painters are runners. Some runners are farmers. Conclusions: I. Some painters are farmers. II. All farmers are painters. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The specified intersections do not force A and C to overlap or include one another.

questions.stem: Statements: Some drivers are pilots. All pilots are sailors. Conclusions: I. Some drivers are sailors. II. All drivers are sailors. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Some A–B members must be C; not all A need be C.

questions.stem: Ritu walks 65 km north, then 52 km east, then 13 km south and finally 13 km west. What is her shortest distance from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Net north = 52 km and east = 39 km. Distance = √(52²+39²) = 65 km.

questions.stem: Kiran moves 13 km north, 78 km east, 39 km south and 13 km west. In which direction is Kiran from the start?

questions.stem: A cyclist travels 117 km north, 52 km east, 65 km south and 13 km west. What total distance did the cyclist travel?
questions.explanation: Total path length = 117+52+65+13=247 km (not displacement).
